speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, how long have you been experiencing these bleeding episodes, and have you noticed any joint pain or swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are there any other family members with similar bleeding tendencies, and has the child had any recent infections or illnesses? I would also like to know if the child has had any surgeries or dental work recently, and how severe the bleeding was in those cases.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any family history of bleeding disorders, such as hemophilia or von Willebrand disease? I would also like to check for any signs of organ enlargement, so may I palpate the abdomen for hepatosplenomegaly?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical issues. Up-to-date on vaccinations. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one older sibling.

speaker: Doctor
text: I do not detect any hepatosplenomegaly on palpation, which makes leukemia less likely. Let's check the platelet count to rule out immune thrombocytopenic purpura. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal)

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the platelet count is normal, I need to evaluate the coagulation cascade. REQUEST TEST: Prothrombin_Time, Partial_Thromboplastin_Time

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal platelets and coagulation times, I suspect a platelet function disorder or von Willebrand disease. REQUEST TEST: Bleeding_Time, Von_Willebrand_Factor_Assay

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bleeding_Time: Prolonged (12 minutes); Von_Willebrand_Factor_Assay: Normal antigen levels and activity

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal vWF assay and prolonged bleeding time, I suspect a platelet function defect like Glanzmann's thrombasthenia. REQUEST TEST: Platelet_Aggregation_Study

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Special_Test: ELISA_Binding_Assay: Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ELISA results confirming a deficiency in GIIb/IIIa receptors are diagnostic. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann's Thrombasthenia
